questions.question: Three persons A, B and C have different amounts of rupees with them. If A takes ₹6 from C, A will have equal amount as B has. A and B together have total ₹74. How many rupees does B have?
questions.solution:
Suppose the amounts with A, B and C are x, y and z respectively.

According to the given information,

A takes ₹6 from C, A will have equal amount as B.

→ x + 6 = y ----(i)

A and B together have total ₹74.

x + y = 74 ----(ii)

Therefore,

x + y = 74

⇒ x + (x + 6) = 74

⇒ 2x + 6 = 74

⇒ 2x = 74 - 6

⇒ 2x = 68

⇒ x = 34.

Therefore, y = 34 + 6 = 40.

So, B has ₹40

Hence, the correct answer is 40.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(2, 4, 8)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

(2, 4, 8) → 2² = 4 and 2³ = 8.

Similarly, 

(4, 16, 64) → 42 = 16 and 43 = 64.

Hence, (4, 16, 64) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the number that is different from the rest.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

1) 13² + 1 = 170

2) 8² + 1 = 65

3) 7² + 1 = 50

**4) 14² - 1 = 195**

Hence, the correct answer is 195.

questions.question:
Two different positions of the same dice are shown below, the six faces of which are numbered 1 to 6. Find the number on the face opposite to the one having ‘5’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52bc0f50aad9163ea9071ac8143adafc9fb619682f8dd6fade35cc293b6ba221.png]
questions.solution:
From the given positions, it can be seen that 2, 3, 4, and 6 are adjacent to 1.

The only number left is 5. Therefore, 1 is opposite to 5.

Hence, 1 will be on the face opposite to the one having 5.

questions.question: ‘Kidney’ is related to ‘Excretion’ in the same way as ‘Heart’ is related to ‘_________’.
questions.solution:

Similarly, the primary function of the heart is blood circulation.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All purses are rupees.

Some rupees are coins.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some purses are coins.

II. No purse is coin.

III. No rupee is coin.

options.text: Only Conclusion I and II follow.
Only Conclusion I and III follow.
Only Conclusion II and III follow.
Either Conclusion I or II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/229470c4e4a4187d6a2e0d825b4101a6c8b39ce45c140708af4c5325c909edcb.png] 

**Solution:**

I. Some purses are coins. → False (it is possible but not definite)

II. No purse is coin. → False (it is possible but not definite)

III. No rupee is coin. → False (Some rupees are coins)

Thus, I and II form a complementary pair.

Hence, either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.
